jobs.name: Emergency locksmith
jobs.title: Emergency Locksmith Leeds: Locked Out? What to Do (2026)
jobs.description: Locked out in Leeds? How an emergency locksmith works, typical night and weekend prices, how to avoid rogue firms and 3 MLA approved local locksmiths.
jobs.h1: Emergency locksmith in Leeds: what to do if you are locked out
jobs.intro: Need an emergency locksmith in Leeds tonight? Before you ring the first number you find, take two minutes to read this. It covers what a fair price looks like, what to ask on the phone and the MLA approved locksmiths we list in Leeds.

sections.h2: Locked out: what to do first
ul: Check every door and window, and whether a neighbour, landlord or family member has a spare key.
If a child or vulnerable person is locked inside, or there is a risk to life, call 999.
If you rent, call your landlord or letting agent first. They may have a key or a locksmith they use.
Check your home insurance. Some policies include home emergency cover for lockouts.

sections.h2: How an emergency locksmith gets you back in
p: Most locksmiths try non destructive entry first. On a uPVC or composite door they may open the multipoint lock without damage, so you only pay for the call out and labour. If the lock cannot be opened this way, the cylinder may need drilling or snapping and replacing. A good locksmith fits a new cylinder before leaving so your home is secure.

sections.h2: How much does an emergency locksmith cost in Leeds?
p: Checkatrade's locksmith price guide (updated May 2026) gives these typical UK figures. Its own Leeds average for a locksmith job is about £149.
ul: Out of hours call out fee: £50 to £150 (average £100)
Out of hours hourly rate: £80 to £200
Midnight to 6am: around £120 an hour
Regain entry to a property: £90 to £130
Broken key removed from a lock: £80 to £100
Emergency boarding up: around £200

sections.h2: How to avoid a rogue locksmith
p: Locksmiths are not regulated in the UK, and some firms advertise in the sponsored results at the top of a search, quote a low price, then charge far more on the doorstep. Get a total price on the phone, including VAT and any new lock. Ask for the locksmith's name and MLA licence number and check it on the Master Locksmiths Association website. If the price changes when they arrive, you can say no.

sections.h2: Emergency locksmiths in Leeds we list
p: All three locksmiths on our locksmiths in Leeds page are MLA approved. Lemon Locksmith says it offers a 24/7 service with no call out charge. Call the firm directly and ask what hours it covers tonight.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to get a locksmith to open a door?
faqs.a: Checkatrade's 2026 guide puts regaining entry at about £90 to £130, plus any out of hours call out fee. A new lock is extra if the old one has to be drilled.

faqs.q: How long do emergency locksmiths take to arrive?
faqs.a: A local locksmith can often reach you within an hour in Leeds, but it depends on the time and where they are. Ask for an arrival time on the phone.

faqs.q: Will my insurance pay for an emergency locksmith?
faqs.a: Only if your policy includes home emergency cover or lost keys cover. Check your policy documents or call your insurer before booking.

faqs.q: Can a locksmith let me into a house I rent?
faqs.a: A good locksmith will ask for proof that you live there, such as ID with the address or a tenancy agreement, before opening the door.

jobs.name: Car locksmith (auto locksmith)
jobs.title: Auto Locksmith Leeds: Lost Car Keys and Lockouts (2026)
jobs.description: Need an auto locksmith in Leeds? What a car locksmith can do for lost keys, lockouts and fobs, when to use a main dealer instead, and local locksmiths.
jobs.h1: Auto locksmith in Leeds: lost car keys and car lockouts
jobs.intro: An auto locksmith in Leeds can get you back into a locked car, cut and programme a new key or fob, and replace a lost key without the car going to a main dealer. Here is what they do, what to ask, and which of the locksmiths we list in Leeds offer car work.

sections.h2: What a car locksmith can do
ul: Open a locked car without damage when the keys are inside
Cut and programme a replacement key or remote fob when all keys are lost
Make a spare key from the one you have
Remove a broken key from the ignition or door lock
Repair a faulty fob, such as a broken case or worn buttons

p: A main dealer can always supply a new key, but you usually need to get the car to them, which can mean a tow if you have lost every key, and you may wait days for the part. An auto locksmith comes to the car and can often programme a key on the spot. For some newer or prestige models only the dealer can supply a key, so ask the locksmith to confirm they can do your make, model and year before they set off.

ul: Your V5C logbook and photo ID, as a reputable car locksmith will want proof you own the car
The make, model, year and registration
Whether you have any working key at all, as copying a key is cheaper than starting from scratch

sections.h2: Car locksmiths in Leeds we list
p: Of the three MLA approved firms on our locksmiths in Leeds page, Lemon Locksmith says it provides an emergency auto locksmith service, car key cutting and car lockouts. The others focus on homes and businesses, so ask before booking. Keys locked in a car with a child or pet inside is an emergency: call 999.

sections.h2: How to avoid paying too much
p: Ask for a fixed price that includes the key blank, cutting, programming and call out. Prices for car keys vary widely by make and the type of key, so a firm that will not quote until it arrives is a warning sign. For home locks, see our locksmith cost guide.

faqs.q: Can a locksmith make a car key without the original?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Many auto locksmiths can cut and programme a new key from the lock or the car's computer, but it depends on the make and model.

faqs.q: Is losing all my car keys a big problem?
faqs.a: It costs more than copying a key, because the new key has to be made and programmed from scratch and old keys removed from the car's memory. It is still usually quicker with an auto locksmith than a dealer.

faqs.q: Do I need the logbook for a new car key?
faqs.a: A reputable locksmith will ask for the V5C logbook and ID to prove the car is yours before making a key.

jobs.name: uPVC door lock repair
jobs.title: uPVC Door Repair Leeds: Locks, Handles and Hinges (2026)
jobs.description: uPVC door repair in Leeds: why doors drop, stick or will not lock, what a locksmith can fix, typical lock prices for 2026 and local firms we list.
jobs.h1: uPVC door repair in Leeds: locks, handles and dropped doors
jobs.intro: A uPVC door that will not lock, a handle that has gone floppy or a key that is hard to turn are common faults in Leeds homes. Most can be fixed by a locksmith or uPVC door repair specialist without replacing the door. Here is what usually goes wrong and what repairs cost.

ul: Handle floppy or will not lift: the gearbox in the multipoint lock is often worn or broken.
Key hard to turn: the door has dropped, so the lock bolts no longer line up with the keeps in the frame.
Door sticks or scrapes: the hinges need adjusting, which is often a quick job.
Draughts: the rubber gasket seal is worn or the door is out of line.
Key snapped in the lock: the cylinder usually needs removing and replacing.

p: Most uPVC door repairs cost far less than a new door. Hinges can be adjusted, the multipoint mechanism replaced and the cylinder upgraded while the door stays in place. Replacement makes sense only if the frame is warped, the door panel is damaged or the door is very old and a matching mechanism cannot be found.

sections.h2: How much does uPVC door lock repair cost?
p: Checkatrade's locksmith price guide (updated May 2026) gives these typical UK figures for uPVC locks:
ul: Change a standard uPVC lock: £100 to £150 (average £125)
Change an anti snap uPVC lock: £125 to £175 (average £150)
Patio door lock replacement: £90 to £100

sections.h2: Upgrade to an anti snap cylinder
p: If your cylinder is being replaced anyway, ask for one rated TS007 3 star or SS312 Diamond. These are designed to resist lock snapping, a common way burglars get through uPVC doors, and some insurers ask for them.

sections.h2: Who fixes uPVC doors in Leeds
p: Locksmiths can repair uPVC locks, mechanisms and cylinders. The Yorkshire Lock and Door Man, on our locksmiths in Leeds list, works on doors as well as locks. For misted glass or a damaged frame you may need a double glazing repair firm instead.

faqs.q: Can a locksmith fix a uPVC door?
faqs.a: Yes. Locksmiths regularly repair uPVC door locks, replace multipoint mechanisms and cylinders, and adjust hinges so the door locks smoothly again.

faqs.q: Why won't my uPVC door lock?
faqs.a: Usually the door has dropped on its hinges, so the bolts do not meet the keeps in the frame. Adjusting the hinges or keeps often fixes it. If the handle will not lift at all, the gearbox may be broken.

faqs.q: How long does a uPVC door repair take?
faqs.a: Many repairs, such as a cylinder change or hinge adjustment, take under an hour. Replacing a full multipoint mechanism can take longer if the part has to be ordered.

jobs.name: Emergency plumber
jobs.title: Emergency Plumber Leeds: Burst Pipes and Leaks (2026)
jobs.description: Need an emergency plumber in Leeds? What to do in the first ten minutes, who to call for gas or water mains problems, and local plumbers we list.
jobs.h1: Emergency plumber in Leeds: burst pipes, leaks and no water
jobs.intro: A burst pipe, water through the ceiling or a toilet that will not stop running. If you need an emergency plumber in Leeds, here is what to do while you wait, when it is not a plumber you need at all, and the local plumbing firms we list.

p: Call an emergency plumber for water you cannot stop: a burst or leaking pipe, a leak through a ceiling, an overflowing toilet or tank, or no water at all because of a fault inside your home. A dripping tap or slow drain can usually wait for a normal appointment, which costs less.

sections.h2: What to do before the plumber arrives
ul: Turn off the water at the stop tap, usually under the kitchen sink or where the pipe enters the house.
Turn off the central heating and boiler if the leak is on the heating system.
If water is near sockets, lights or the fuse board, switch off the electrics at the consumer unit if it is safe to reach.
Open cold taps to drain the pipes, and catch drips with buckets and towels.
Take photos for your home insurance.

sections.h2: When it is not a plumber you need
ul: Smell of gas: leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999.
Leak in the street or before your stop tap: this is usually the water company's pipe. Leeds is supplied by Yorkshire Water.
Shared drain blocked outside: drains shared with neighbours are usually the water company's responsibility.
Council or housing association tenants: report it to your landlord's emergency repairs line first.

sections.h2: Choosing an emergency plumber in Leeds
p: Ask for the call out fee and hourly rate before they set off, and whether parts are extra. For anything involving a gas boiler, the engineer must be on the Gas Safe Register. See our plumbers in Leeds list for three local plumbing and heating firms, including Same Day Plumber Leeds, which offers 24/7 call outs.

ul: Know where your stop tap is and check it turns.
Lag pipes in lofts, garages and outside walls before winter.
Get your boiler serviced once a year by a Gas Safe engineer.
Do not pour fat or wipes down sinks and toilets.

faqs.q: How quickly can an emergency plumber get to me in Leeds?
faqs.a: It depends on the time of day and how busy they are. Local firms can often arrive within one to two hours. Ask for a time on the phone.

faqs.q: Who do I call for a burst water main in Leeds?
faqs.a: A leak in the road or pavement, or before your stop tap, is usually the water company's responsibility. In Leeds that is Yorkshire Water.

faqs.q: Can a plumber fix my boiler in an emergency?
faqs.a: Only if they are a Gas Safe registered engineer qualified for boilers. Many Leeds plumbing firms offer both, but always ask.

faqs.q: Should I turn the water off if a pipe bursts?
faqs.a: Yes. Turn off the stop tap straight away to limit the damage, then call a plumber.

jobs.name: Artex and asbestos ceiling removal
jobs.title: Artex Removal Leeds: Asbestos Ceilings Tested and Removed
jobs.description: Artex removal in Leeds: how to find out if your Artex ceiling contains asbestos, removal versus covering it, typical 2026 costs and local firms.
jobs.h1: Artex removal in Leeds: asbestos ceilings and textured coatings
jobs.intro: Thinking of removing an Artex ceiling in Leeds? Artex and similar textured coatings applied before 2000 can contain a small amount of asbestos. Here is how to find out, your options, what removal costs and the asbestos firms we list in Leeds.

p: Textured coatings like Artex were used on ceilings and walls for decades, and some made before the late 1980s contain white asbestos (chrysotile). You cannot tell by looking. The only way to know is to have a small sample tested by a lab. See asbestos testing in Leeds.

ul: Leave it: Artex in good condition that you are not disturbing is low risk.
Cover it: overboard with plasterboard or have a plasterer skim over it, without sanding or scraping first.
Remove it: needed if the ceiling is coming down or being rewired heavily. It must be done with controls to stop fibres spreading.

sections.h2: Never sand or scrape Artex that might contain asbestos
p: Sanding, dry scraping or drilling textured coatings releases fibres into the room. If you do not know whether it contains asbestos, treat it as if it does until it has been tested.

sections.h2: How much does Artex removal cost?
p: Checkatrade's asbestos removal guide (updated February 2026) puts domestic removal of Artex ceilings and asbestos tiles at £175 to £350 per square metre, averaging £225, and removing an asbestos Artex ceiling from a 20 square metre room at about £2,750 to £6,000. Covering it over is often far cheaper. See our asbestos removal cost guide.
The firms on our asbestos removal in Leeds page can test and remove textured coatings. Ask how they will contain the area, how waste will be bagged and where it will go.

faqs.q: How do I know if Artex has asbestos?
faqs.a: Only a lab test of a sample can tell you. Artex applied before 2000, and especially before the late 1980s, is more likely to contain it.

faqs.q: Can I plaster over Artex?
faqs.a: Yes. A plasterer can skim or overboard Artex without disturbing it, which avoids removal. They must not sand or scrape it first.

faqs.q: Is Artex with asbestos dangerous?
faqs.a: It is low risk while intact and undisturbed. The risk comes from sanding, scraping or drilling it.

jobs.name: Roof repair
jobs.title: Roof Repair Leeds: Leaks, Slipped Tiles and Flashing (2026)
jobs.description: Roof repair in Leeds: common roof leaks on Leeds terraces, what a roofer checks, repair or replace, and local roofers we list.
jobs.h1: Roof repair in Leeds: leaks, slipped slates and flashing
jobs.intro: A drip in the loft, a damp patch on the ceiling or slates on the path after a storm. Most roof leaks in Leeds are fixable with a repair rather than a new roof. Here is what usually goes wrong, what to ask a roofer and the local roofers we list.

ul: Slipped or cracked slates and tiles, often after high winds
Failed lead flashing around chimneys and where roofs meet walls
Chimney stacks with loose pointing or cracked flaunching
Valleys and gutters blocked with moss and leaves
Flat roofs on extensions and dormers with split felt

sections.h2: Roof repairs we see most in Leeds
p: Leeds has a lot of older terraced and semi detached houses with slate roofs, and many extensions and dormers with flat roofs. Roof repair jobs for roofing companies in Leeds and the surrounding areas often include replacing slipped slates and tiles, renewing lead flashing, repointing chimneys, clearing gutters and patching or replacing flat roofs. A good roofer will explain the cause of the roof damage, not just patch the symptom.

sections.h2: What to do about a leak now
ul: Put a bucket under the drip and move valuables.
If water is near light fittings, switch off that circuit.
Take photos for your insurer.
Do not go on the roof yourself.

p: A few slipped slates or a section of flashing is a repair. If a roofer finds widespread slipped slates from nail fatigue, rotten battens or a roof leaking in several places, replacement may be better value. See our roof replacement cost guide for 2026 prices.

ul: What exactly is causing the leak?
Do you need scaffolding, or can you use a ladder or roof ladder?
Is there a guarantee on the repair?
Will you send photos of the problem and the finished repair?

p: See our list of roofers in Leeds for three local firms with the checks we have made. For flat roofs, ask specifically about felt, EPDM rubber or GRP fibreglass experience.

faqs.q: Can a roof be repaired in the rain?
faqs.a: A roofer can often make a temporary repair, such as a tarpaulin, in bad weather, with the permanent fix once it is dry.

faqs.q: Will my insurance cover a roof repair?
faqs.a: Storm damage is often covered, wear and tear usually is not. Take photos and call your insurer before major work.

faqs.q: Do I need scaffolding for a roof repair?
faqs.a: Not always. Small repairs can often be done with a roof ladder. Chimneys and larger repairs usually need scaffolding or a tower.

faqs.q: How long does a roof repair take?
faqs.a: Small repairs such as replacing a few slates are often done in a few hours. Chimney work or larger repairs that need scaffolding can take a few days.

jobs.name: Emergency electrician
jobs.title: Emergency Electrician Leeds: Power Cuts and Tripping (2026)
jobs.description: Emergency electrician in Leeds: what to check before calling, when it is a power cut, what an emergency call costs and local registered electricians.
jobs.h1: Emergency electrician in Leeds: no power, tripping and burning smells
jobs.intro: Lost power, a fuse board that keeps tripping, a burning smell or a socket that sparked. If you need an emergency electrician in Leeds, check these first, as some problems are not yours to fix, and then call a registered electrician.

p: If your neighbours have no power too, it is likely a power cut. In Leeds, call 105, the free national power cut number, to reach the local network operator. An electrician cannot fix a fault on the network.

ul: Look for a switch or RCD that has tripped to off.
Switch everything off, reset the main switch, then turn circuits back on one by one.
If one circuit trips straight away, unplug everything on it and try again. A faulty appliance is a common cause.
If it still trips, leave it off and call an electrician.

sections.h2: When to call an emergency electrician
ul: A burning smell, scorch marks or smoke from a socket, switch or the consumer unit
A circuit that trips and will not reset with appliances unplugged
Water leaking near electrics
Exposed or damaged wiring
No power to the whole home when neighbours have power

sections.h2: What does an emergency electrician cost?
p: Checkatrade's 2026 guide gives a typical electrician rate of £40 to £70 an hour plus VAT, averaging £55. Evening, night and weekend call outs usually cost more. Ask for the call out fee and hourly rate before they come.
Check the electrician is registered with a scheme such as NICEIC or NAPIT so the work can be certified. See our list of electricians in Leeds.

sections.h2: Electrical faults that need an emergency electrician
p: Most emergency electrician call outs in Leeds are for a circuit that keeps tripping, a fuse box or consumer unit fault, a socket or switch that has overheated, or water leaking onto electrics. These faults can cause a fire or an electric shock, so turn off power to the affected circuit if you can do it safely and do not use it again until it has been checked.

sections.h2: Choosing an emergency electrician in Leeds
ul: Ask whether the electrician is registered with NICEIC or NAPIT, so any repair can be certified under Part P of the Building Regulations.
Ask for the emergency call out fee and the hourly rate before they come, including evenings and weekends.
Ask whether they carry common parts, such as RCDs and breakers, so the fault can be fixed on the first visit.
Ask for a written report of what was found and fixed.

p: If the fault was caused by old wiring, the electrician may recommend an EICR, an inspection of the whole installation. Landlords must have one at least every 5 years. See our EICR cost guide for 2026 prices, and our list of electricians in Leeds, including Martin Day Electricians, for planned work.

faqs.q: What number do I call for a power cut in Leeds?
faqs.a: Call 105, the free national power cut number. It puts you through to your local electricity network operator.

faqs.q: Why does my electric keep tripping?
faqs.a: Usually a faulty appliance, water in a socket or light, or a damaged cable. Unplug everything on the circuit and reset it. If it still trips, call an electrician.

faqs.q: Is a burning smell from a socket an emergency?
faqs.a: Yes. Switch off at the consumer unit if it is safe to do so, stop using the socket and call an electrician. If there is smoke or fire, call 999.

faqs.q: Can I get a 24 hour emergency electrician in Leeds?
faqs.a: Some Leeds electricians offer 24 hour call outs, usually at a higher rate at night and weekends. Ask for the price before they set off.

faqs.q: Should I call an electrician or the power company?
faqs.a: If your neighbours have also lost power, call 105 for the network operator. If only your home or one circuit is affected, call an electrician.

jobs.name: Asbestos testing (samples and lab tests)
jobs.title: Asbestos Testing Leeds: Sample Tests and Lab Results (2026)
jobs.description: Asbestos testing in Leeds: when a single sample test is enough, how sampling works, typical 2026 costs and local firms that test for asbestos.
jobs.h1: Asbestos testing in Leeds: samples and lab results
jobs.intro: Not sure if your garage roof, Artex ceiling or floor tiles contain asbestos? Asbestos testing in Leeds usually means a surveyor takes a small sample and sends it to a lab. Here is when a test is enough, what it costs and which firms we list.

p: A sample test answers one question: does this material contain asbestos? It suits a single item such as a garage roof, a ceiling or a boxed in pipe. If you are planning building work across a room or a whole house, you need a survey instead. See asbestos surveys in Leeds.

ul: A trained surveyor wets the material, takes a small piece and seals it in a bag.
The sample point is sealed so fibres are not released.
The sample goes to a laboratory, ideally UKAS accredited.
You get a written result, usually within a few days.

sections.h2: How much does asbestos testing cost?
p: MyBuilder's 2026 guide puts standard sampling at about £50 per sample and comprehensive lab analysis at £100 to £250. DIY kits cost £35 to £50, but you take the sample yourself, which carries a risk. See our asbestos survey cost guide.

sections.h2: What to do with the result
p: If the test is negative, you can carry on with your work. If it is positive, decide whether to leave, seal or remove the material. For removal, see asbestos removal in Leeds.

sections.h2: Where asbestos is found in Leeds homes
ul: Garage and shed roofs made of asbestos cement
Artex and other textured coatings on ceilings
Floor tiles and the bitumen adhesive under them
Boxing around pipes and boilers, and old boiler flues
Soffits and panels under windows on some post war houses

p: Look for a surveyor or asbestos company that sends samples to a UKAS accredited laboratory and gives a written result. Several firms on our list, including Yorkshire Asbestos Solutions, offer testing as well as surveys and removal.

faqs.q: How long do asbestos test results take?
faqs.a: Usually a few days after the sample reaches the lab. Some labs offer faster results for a higher fee.

faqs.q: Can I take an asbestos sample myself?
faqs.a: Kits are sold for this, but taking a sample can release fibres. A trained surveyor will take it safely and seal the area.

faqs.q: Do I need to test an asbestos garage roof before removal?
faqs.a: It is sensible. Many removal firms ask for a test result before they quote, as it confirms the right method and disposal.

jobs.name: Damp survey
jobs.title: Damp Survey Leeds: What It Checks and What It Costs (2026)
jobs.description: Damp survey in Leeds: what an independent damp survey checks, free versus paid surveys, typical 2026 prices and local damp specialists.
jobs.h1: Damp survey in Leeds: find the cause before you pay for treatment
jobs.intro: A damp survey in Leeds tells you what kind of damp you have and why, before anyone sells you a treatment. Here is what a good survey includes, the difference between free and independent surveys, and what one costs.

ul: Where the damp is and how far it spreads
Moisture readings, ideally checked with other tests, not a meter alone
Outside causes: gutters, downpipes, pointing, render, ground levels and air bricks
Ventilation and heating, to rule condensation in or out
Timber condition, for rot or woodworm

p: Many damp proofing companies offer a free survey. That is not always bad, but the surveyor is usually also selling the treatment. An independent survey from a surveyor who does not sell treatment costs more but gives you a neutral view. For a house purchase, your mortgage lender may ask for a specific damp and timber report.

sections.h2: How much does a damp survey cost?
p: MyBuilder's 2026 guide puts damp surveys at £150 to £500, with a basic visual survey at £150 to £250 and a comprehensive survey with thermal imaging at £200 to £500. By property it gives about £180 to £250 for a terraced house and £200 to £300 for a semi. See our damp survey cost guide.
See our list of damp proofing firms in Leeds. Ask each one whether the survey is free, what tests it includes and whether you get a written report.

faqs.q: Is a free damp survey worth having?
faqs.a: It can be useful, but remember the surveyor may also be selling the treatment. If the quote is large, consider a second opinion or an independent survey.

faqs.q: How long does a damp survey take?
faqs.a: Usually one to two hours for a typical house, with a written report afterwards.

faqs.q: Can a damp survey tell rising damp from condensation?
faqs.a: A good one should. It will look at where the damp is, salts on the plaster, outside defects and ventilation, not just moisture readings.

jobs.name: Rising damp treatment
jobs.title: Rising Damp Leeds: Signs, Causes and Treatment (2026)
jobs.description: Rising damp in Leeds: how to recognise it, the common causes in stone terraces, treatment options and what to check before you pay for a damp course.
jobs.h1: Rising damp in Leeds: signs, causes and treatment
jobs.intro: Rising damp is water drawn up from the ground through a wall. It is often blamed for damp in Leeds homes, but it is less common than condensation or leaks. Here is how to recognise it, what causes it and the treatment options.

ul: A tide mark on internal walls up to about a metre above the floor
White salts or crumbling plaster low on the wall
Peeling paint or lifting wallpaper at skirting level
Damp or rotting skirting boards and floor timbers
Ground or path levels outside raised above the damp proof course
Render or pointing that bridges the damp proof course
Old houses built with no damp proof course at all
Blocked air bricks under suspended timber floors
Cement plaster that traps moisture in solid stone walls

p: The first step is often the cheapest: lower the ground level outside, clear air bricks and remove anything bridging the damp course. Where a new damp proof course is needed, specialists usually inject a cream into the mortar. The wall then needs to dry, and salt damaged plaster is often replaced. Ask the surveyor to explain why the chosen treatment fits your wall.
Because rising damp is often misdiagnosed, start with a damp survey in Leeds and get the cause in writing. For local specialists, see damp proofing in Leeds.

sections.h2: Rising damp, penetrating damp or condensation?
p: Many damp problems in Leeds are diagnosed as rising damp when the real cause is penetrating damp from a leaking gutter or failed pointing, or condensation and mould from poor ventilation. A specialist damp survey should rule each one in or out. Musty smells, mould on cold walls and damp patches high on the wall usually point away from rising damp.

sections.h2: Timber decay, woodworm and dry rot
p: Damp walls can lead to timber decay in skirting boards, joists and floor timbers. Wet rot, dry rot and woodworm are all more likely where timber stays damp. A damp and timber survey checks for these too, and a damp proofing specialist in Leeds will usually offer woodworm treatment and dry rot treatment alongside damp proofing.

sections.h2: Questions to ask a damp proofer
ul: How have you diagnosed rising damp rather than another type of damp?
Is the existing damp proof course (DPC) failed, bridged or missing?
What will you do about salt damaged plaster?
Is the guarantee insurance backed?
How long before I can decorate?

faqs.q: Is rising damp common?
faqs.a: It is less common than condensation or penetrating damp. Many damp problems blamed on rising damp are caused by leaks, bridging or poor ventilation.

faqs.q: Can I fix rising damp myself?
faqs.a: You can often reduce it by lowering ground levels outside and clearing air bricks. A new chemical damp proof course is usually a specialist job.

faqs.q: How long does a wall take to dry after damp proofing?
faqs.a: Solid walls can take months to dry fully. Your specialist should explain when it is safe to replaster and decorate.

faqs.q: How much does rising damp treatment cost?
faqs.a: It depends on the length of wall, the treatment and the replastering needed. Get a written quote after a survey, and compare at least two damp proofing firms.

jobs.name: Condensation and ventilation (PIV)
jobs.title: Condensation Leeds: Mould, Ventilation and PIV Units (2026)
jobs.description: Condensation and black mould in Leeds homes: why it happens, simple fixes, extractor fans and PIV units, and when to call a damp specialist.
jobs.h1: Condensation and mould in Leeds: ventilation and PIV units
jobs.intro: Wet windows every morning and black mould in the corners are signs of condensation, the most common cause of damp in Leeds homes. Here is why it happens, what you can do yourself and when ventilation such as a PIV unit helps.

p: Cooking, showering, breathing and drying clothes put moisture into the air. When that warm moist air meets a cold surface, such as a window, an outside wall or a corner behind a wardrobe, it turns to water. Older solid wall houses in Leeds have cold walls, so condensation and mould are common in winter.

ul: Use extractor fans or open a window when cooking and showering.
Dry clothes outside or in a vented dryer where you can.
Keep a steady low heat rather than short bursts.
Leave a gap between furniture and outside walls.
Wipe windows each morning and clean mould with a suitable product.
Extractor fans in the kitchen and bathroom, ideally with a humidity sensor
Trickle vents in window frames
PIV (positive input ventilation): a unit, often in the loft, that gently pushes filtered air into the home, displacing moist air
Heat recovery units for single rooms

p: If mould keeps coming back despite good habits, or you are not sure the damp is condensation, get a damp survey in Leeds. Many damp firms on our damp proofing in Leeds list also fit ventilation.

sections.h2: Condensation, rising damp or penetrating damp?
p: Condensation causes damp and mould on cold surfaces, often worst in bedrooms, bathrooms and north facing rooms in winter. Rising damp shows low on walls with a tide mark and salts. Penetrating damp appears after rain, often near gutters, windows or chimneys. Getting the cause right matters, because damp proofing does not fix condensation.

Black mould growth from condensation can affect people with asthma, allergies and weak immune systems. Clean small areas of mould on hard surfaces with a suitable product, wearing gloves, and deal with the cause. If you rent in Leeds and mould keeps returning, report it to your landlord in writing.

Many Leeds damp specialists offer condensation control as well as damp proofing, fitting PIV units, humidity controlled extractor fans and ventilation in lofts and bathrooms. Ask for a survey first, and see our list of damp proofing in Leeds.

faqs.q: What is a PIV unit?
faqs.a: Positive input ventilation draws air in, filters it and gently pushes it into the home, usually from the loft. It helps move moist air out and can reduce condensation.

faqs.q: Is condensation my landlord's problem?
faqs.a: Landlords must deal with serious damp and mould hazards, including fixing faults that cause condensation, such as broken fans. Report it in writing.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier stop condensation?
faqs.a: It helps by removing moisture from the air, especially when drying clothes indoors. It works best alongside ventilation.

jobs.name: Wasp nest removal
jobs.title: Wasp Nest Removal Leeds: Prices and What to Do (2026)
jobs.description: Wasp nest removal in Leeds: when to treat a nest, why not to do it yourself, typical 2026 prices and local pest controllers including the council.
jobs.h1: Wasp nest removal in Leeds: what to do and what it costs
jobs.intro: A wasp nest in the loft, under the eaves or in a bush near the door. Wasp nest removal in Leeds is usually a quick treatment by a pest controller. Here is when to treat, what it costs and who to call.

sections.h2: Do you need to remove it?
p: Wasp nests die off naturally by late autumn and are not reused. If a nest is out of the way and nobody is allergic, you can leave it. Treat it if it is near a door, window, path or play area, or if anyone in the home has a known allergy to stings.

Disturbing a nest can provoke many wasps at once. A pest controller uses protective gear and an insecticide dust or spray at the nest entrance, and the nest usually dies within a day or two. Bees are different: they are not usually destroyed, so a pest controller will identify them first.

sections.h2: How much does wasp nest removal cost?
p: Checkatrade's 2026 guide puts wasp control for one nest at about £75 to £200, averaging £137.50. Leeds City Council also treats wasps for residents, though its standard all visits price does not apply to wasps. See our pest control cost guide.

sections.h2: Pest controllers in Leeds we list
p: See our pest control in Leeds page. MJR Pest Control says it offers same day response for wasps.

faqs.q: How much is wasp nest removal in Leeds?
faqs.a: Checkatrade's 2026 guide gives about £75 to £200 for one nest, averaging £137.50.

faqs.q: How long does it take for a wasp nest to die after treatment?
faqs.a: Usually within a day or two. Keep away from the entrance while the treatment works.

faqs.q: Will a pest controller remove bees?
faqs.a: Bees are not usually destroyed. A pest controller can identify them and may refer you to a beekeeper.

jobs.name: House clearance
jobs.title: House Clearance Leeds: How It Works and What to Ask (2026)
jobs.description: House clearance in Leeds: how a full house clearance works, sorting items to keep, donate or recycle, waste licence checks and local clearance firms.
jobs.h1: House clearance in Leeds: full and part house clearances
jobs.intro: Clearing a house after a bereavement, a move into care or the end of a tenancy is a big job. A house clearance firm in Leeds can empty the property, sort what can be reused and dispose of the rest legally. Here is how it works and what to ask.

ul: A free visit or video call to see the property and agree a price
Removing anything you want to keep first, plus paperwork and valuables
Sorting items to sell, donate, recycle or dispose of
Clearing lofts, garages, sheds and gardens if agreed
Sweeping or cleaning the property afterwards, if included

p: You can be held responsible if your waste is fly tipped. Check the clearance firm's waste carrier registration with the Environment Agency and keep the receipt or waste transfer note.

Furniture in good condition can sometimes be resold or donated, which some firms offset against the price. Removing items you want to keep and anything of value before the visit helps the firm give a fixed price.

sections.h2: Clearance firms in Leeds we list
p: See our list of rubbish removal and house clearance in Leeds. For a big clear out over several days, a skip may be cheaper.

sections.h2: What a house clearance usually includes
p: A full house clearance in Leeds normally covers furniture, white goods, carpets, kitchen items, clothes and loft and garage contents. Some clearance firms also offer a deep clean afterwards, which is useful at the end of a tenancy or before a sale. Garden waste and sheds may be extra.

ul: Ask for a free visit or send photos of every room, loft and garage.
Ask for a fixed price, not an estimate by the van load.
Ask what will be recycled or donated and what goes to landfill.
Check whether the price includes VAT and disposal charges for fridges and mattresses.

faqs.q: How long does a house clearance take?
faqs.a: A typical house is often cleared in one or two days, depending on how full it is and whether there is a loft or garage.

faqs.q: Do house clearance firms take everything?
faqs.a: Most take furniture and general household items. Fridges, mattresses, paint and asbestos may cost extra or need separate disposal.

faqs.q: Can a house clearance firm help after a bereavement?
faqs.a: Yes. Many work with executors and families, and will set aside paperwork, photos and valuables they find.

faqs.q: How much does a house clearance cost in Leeds?
faqs.a: It depends on how much there is and access. Get two or three fixed quotes after a visit. Our house clearance cost guide is coming in a later update.

jobs.name: Shed and outbuilding removal
jobs.title: Shed Removal Leeds: Sheds, Greenhouses and Outbuildings (2026)
jobs.description: Shed removal in Leeds: dismantling and taking away old sheds, greenhouses and small outbuildings, what to check for asbestos, and local firms.
jobs.h1: Shed removal in Leeds: old sheds and outbuildings taken away
jobs.intro: An old timber shed, a broken greenhouse or a small outbuilding taking up the garden. Shed removal in Leeds is usually a half day job for a clearance or demolition firm. Here is what is involved and what to check first.

ul: Emptying the shed, or arranging for contents to be cleared too
Dismantling the walls, roof and floor
Taking away the timber, felt and glass for disposal
Lifting a concrete or slab base if you want it gone

p: Timber sheds rarely contain asbestos, but older concrete sheds, outhouses and some roofs can have asbestos cement sheets. If in doubt, have it tested first. See asbestos testing in Leeds.

For a timber shed, a rubbish removal or clearance firm is usually the cheapest option. See rubbish removal in Leeds. For brick or concrete outbuildings and garages, see our garage removal in Leeds list.

sections.h2: Shed removal or full garden clearance?
p: Many people clear a shed at the same time as other garden waste, old fencing or a broken greenhouse. A rubbish removal firm can usually take all of it in one visit, which is often cheaper than separate jobs. If you are replacing the shed, ask whether the new shed supplier will take the old one away.

ul: Is the price for dismantling and removal, or removal only?
Will you lift the base and leave the area level?
Do you hold a waste carrier registration?
What happens to the timber and glass?

faqs.q: How long does it take to remove a shed?
faqs.a: A standard timber shed is often removed in a few hours. Larger outbuildings or concrete bases take longer.

faqs.q: Can I put an old shed in a skip?
faqs.a: Timber and felt can usually go in a skip. Asbestos sheets and glass may need separate handling.

jobs.name: Mini skip hire
jobs.title: Mini Skip Hire Leeds: Sizes, Prices and Permits (2026)
jobs.description: Mini skip hire in Leeds: what fits in a 2 or 3 yard skip, typical 2026 prices in the north, Leeds permit rules and local skip firms.
jobs.h1: Mini skip hire in Leeds: 2 and 3 yard skips
jobs.intro: A mini skip is the smallest skip most firms hire, usually 2 or 3 cubic yards. It suits a garden tidy, a small bathroom refit or a clear out. Here is what fits, what mini skip hire in Leeds costs and whether you need a permit.

sections.h2: What fits in a mini skip
p: A 2 to 3 yard mini skip typically holds around 20 to 30 bin bags of waste. It is ideal for garden waste, a small bathroom or a single room clear out. It is small enough for many drives, which can avoid a road permit.

sections.h2: How much does a mini skip cost?
p: Checkatrade's 2026 guide puts a 2 to 3 yard skip in the north of England at about £65 to £110 a week, and the UK average at £125. MyBuilder gives £95 to £145 for mini skips. See our skip hire cost guide for Leeds.
Not if the skip goes on your drive or private land. On a road or pavement in Leeds, a registered skip company must apply to Leeds City Council for a licence, and a fee applies.
See our list of skip hire in Leeds for three local firms. If you only have a few bags, a rubbish removal collection may be cheaper.

faqs.q: How many bags fit in a mini skip?
faqs.a: Roughly 20 to 30 bin bags for a 2 to 3 yard skip, depending on what you put in.

faqs.q: Can a mini skip go on the road in Leeds?
faqs.a: Yes, with a council licence applied for by a registered skip company.

jobs.name: Grab hire and wait and load
jobs.title: Grab Hire Leeds: Grab Lorries and Wait and Load (2026)
jobs.description: Grab hire in Leeds: when a grab lorry beats a skip for soil and rubble, wait and load explained, access and local firms to ask.
jobs.h1: Grab hire and wait and load in Leeds
jobs.intro: Got a pile of soil, rubble or hardcore to shift? Grab hire in Leeds uses a lorry with a crane arm that lifts waste straight off your drive, with no skip left behind. Wait and load is a similar idea for a skip. Here is when each makes sense.

p: A grab lorry has a hydraulic arm with a bucket that reaches over walls and fences and lifts loose waste such as soil, rubble and hardcore. You pile the waste up, the lorry arrives, loads it and leaves. It suits landscaping, driveway digs and extension groundworks.

With wait and load, a skip lorry drops a skip and waits while you fill it, then takes it away, usually within an hour or so. It avoids a road permit and stops neighbours using your skip. MyBuilder puts wait and load at about £20 to £50 on top of the skip price.

sections.h2: Grab, skip or wait and load?
ul: Grab hire: best for large loads of heavy loose waste you can pile up first
Wait and load: best when you can fill a skip quickly and have no space to leave one
Skip hire: best for mixed waste over several days

p: Bill Dyson Skip Hire and Jeff Skinner Skip Hire, on our skip hire in Leeds list, both say they offer wait and load. Ask skip firms whether they run grab lorries too.

sections.h2: Grab lorries for muck away and aggregates
p: Grab lorries are often called grab wagons or tipper grabs. As well as muck away, taking soil and rubble off site, many grab hire firms around Leeds and West Yorkshire also deliver aggregates such as sand, gravel and type 1 sub base, tipping or placing it with the same hydraulic arm. That makes grab hire popular with landscapers and on small construction sites.

ul: The size of the grab lorry and the amount of waste in tonnes
The type of waste: clean soil and hardcore usually cost less to dispose of than mixed waste
How far the lorry has to travel from its yard, for example from Bradford or Wakefield into Leeds
Whether the arm can reach the pile from the road, or the lorry must come onto your drive

p: It is worth getting quotes from two or three grab hire firms. Tell them roughly how much waste you have, what it is, where it is piled and how close the lorry can park. A photo helps them confirm the right lorry. Ask whether the price includes tipping fees and VAT, and whether there is a charge if the lorry has to wait.

faqs.q: How much waste can a grab lorry take?
faqs.a: It varies by lorry, so ask the firm for the load in tonnes or cubic yards before booking.

faqs.q: Does grab hire need a permit?
faqs.a: Not usually, because nothing is left on the road. The lorry does need safe access and space to park while it loads.

faqs.q: Is grab hire cheaper than a skip?
faqs.a: For large amounts of soil, rubble or green waste, grab hire is often cheaper than several skips, because one grab lorry can take more weight and nothing is left on the road.

faqs.q: Can a grab lorry reach over a wall?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The hydraulic arm can reach several metres over walls and fences, so the lorry can often load from the road. Ask the firm for the reach of its lorry.
